cases.name: Caliyah JoLynn Guyton
cases.about: Her Go Fund Me said, "She was only 2 years old but had the biggest brightest personality. Caliyah had eyes that would light up a room and a smile that brought joy to anyone that knew her. She was loved by her parents, aunts, uncles, grandparents, cousins and everyone that knew her. She brought so much joy and happiness and a sense of home to everyone that knew her. Caliyah loved Minnie Mouse and baby shark. She loved different animals and exploring and learning new things. She will always be loved and missed."

cases.name: Kendra Diane Livesay Smith
cases.about:
She was a first grade teacher at Coolidge Elementary in Enid, OK. A family friend described Kendra Smith as a "beautiful person inside and out." In a letter sent to staff Wednesday night, the superintendent described her as a cherished part of their school family.

Her obituary said, "She was raised in Guymon, attending the Guymon school system graduating with the Class of 1992. Kendra then attended Southwestern Oklahoma State University and Panhandle State University, earning her bachelor degree in elementary education.

Kendra was a devoted educator with Enid Public Schools, currently teaching at Coolidge Elementary as a first-grade teacher. She also served at Leonardo's Children's Museum in their Discovery After-School and Discovery Camp programs. Her love and encouragement for students has made an impact in so many lives and her legacy and love will live on in all that she has touched. In addition to her love for elementary education, Kendra loved dance and teaching it to others. Her kindness, encouraging words and loving smile will continue to be a bright light for others."
